title: Understanding KDE Plot
text: A Kernel Density Estimate (KDE) plot is used to visualize the distribution of data. It can sometimes resemble a normal distribution if not properly adjusted.

title: Normal Kernel in KDE
text: Using a normal kernel in KDE can make the plot look like a normal distribution, especially if the bandwidth is not adjusted correctly.

hintAnswer: The plot may smooth out the data too much, making it look like a normal distribution.
title: Check Bandwidth
text: What happens if the bandwidth in a KDE plot is too large?
choices: The plot may smooth out the data too much, making it look like a normal distribution.
The plot may become too jagged and not resemble any distribution.

hintAnswer: If the bandwidth is too large, it can smooth out the peaks, making the distribution appear unimodal.
title: Multimodal Distribution
text: Why might a multimodal distribution appear unimodal in a KDE plot?
choices: If the bandwidth is too large, it can smooth out the peaks, making the distribution appear unimodal.
If the bandwidth is too small, it can create artificial peaks.
